activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Madelyn wanted to build a house for her toy sheep. She looked at her blocks. Some blocks were squares. Some were triangles. Some were rectangles. Some were balls, round like circles.

She put a ball on the floor first. Then she put a square block on top. The block slid off. The round ball rolled away. "Oh no," said Madelyn. "The sheep has no wall."

She put the square block down instead. It sat flat and still. She stacked another square on it. Then another. The wall stood tall. The round ball had rolled because it was round. The flat square did not roll. It stayed.

Madelyn made four walls. On top she put a triangle, like a little roof. Under the roof, the sheep fit just right. "Your house is not weak," Madelyn told the sheep. "It is strong."

The sheep sat in its square house. Madelyn smiled and patted the triangle roof.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Raphael was at school. He made a real clay star. It had five points. His teacher Mia smiled at it.

Then Ben grabbed the star. It fell and broke. Raphael made angry fists. His face went hot. "You broke my star," he said. Mia knelt down beside him.

"Why is my face hot?" Raphael asked. "Because you are angry," said Mia. "Big breaths can help." Raphael took a big breath. Then another. His fists let go. His face felt cool again.

Ben said sorry. He helped fix the star. The glue made the points fit back on. The star was whole again.

Raphael jumped up and down. "I feel excited!" he said. Mia laughed. "Me too," she said. She put the real clay star on the shelf, up high, where it would be safe.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Everett sat at the dinner table. He wanted the sweet corn. It was summer corn, his favorite.

"Close your eyes," said Dad. Everett closed his eyes. He could not see the corn. He peeked with one eye. There it was, yellow and bumpy.

Then Everett held his nose. He took a bite. He froze. "I can't taste it!" The corn tasted like nothing at all.

Dad laughed. "Let go of your nose, silly boy." Everett let go. Now the corn tasted sweet again.

"Your nose helps you taste," said Everett. He sniffed the corn with his nose. He listened to it crunch with his ears. He felt the rough little kernels with his fingers.

"I need my whole face for corn," said Everett. Dad laughed and gave him one more piece.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Lennon spotted the red crayons on the shelf. They were up too high. She wanted the red one for her apple picture.

She pulled a chair and stood on it. The chair wobbled. It tipped over. Blocks fell everywhere and her elbow hit Omar's tower. "Sorry, Omar," she said. Omar nodded and started to build again.

Lennon looked up at the shelf. How could she reach now? Miss Ada had a phone on her desk. Maybe that could help? "Miss Ada, can you help me, please?" Lennon asked. Miss Ada smiled and got the red crayon down. "Thank you," said Lennon. She drew a big red apple. "The magic word made it come down," she said. Then she put the chair back where it belonged. "I did it all by myself," she said, "with a little help."

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Cooper sat in the middle of the car. His cup fell on the floor. It rolled far, far away.

"Can you help me, please?" Cooper asked. "Yes, I can help," said Dad. Dad reached back. He got the cup.

Dad bumped Cooper's knee. "Sorry," said Dad. "It's okay," said Cooper.

Cooper drank his water. "Thank you," he said. Dad smiled. "You said please, and I heard you," said Dad. "That is why I could help."

The car was quiet now. Cooper looked out the window. "One red car," he said. "One blue truck. One big bus." Dad laughed at the window game.

"Where is the sun?" Cooper asked. Then he answered himself. "The sun went to sleep. Night is coming." Cooper held his cup tight. Dad patted his knee softly. Cooper watched the cars go by, all the way home.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Gabriella went to the old community kitchen with her dad. Today she would bake banana bread for the whole family. She pulled her stool up to the big counter.

First she needed butter. The butter was cold from the fridge. Gabriella poked it with her finger. It was hard as a rock. She tried to stir it into the bowl. Little hard lumps hid in the mix. "Why won't it mix?" she asked. Her dad said, "Let's wait a bit."

They set the butter on the warm counter. They peeled the bananas, soft and sweet. They looked at the river out the window. They waited some more. Then Gabriella poked the butter again. Now her finger went right in. She stirred it, and it went smooth as a river.

The old kitchen smelled warm and sweet. The bread came out golden brown. Gabriella clapped her hands. "The butter got soft because it waited in the warm!" she said. "Now we can eat!"

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Rowan wanted to make a sandwich. The bread was square. He put it on the plate. Round cheese would not stay on the square bread. It slid and slid. Then the cheese fell off. It made the milk spill. "Oh no," said Rowan.

His mom helped him wipe the milk. "Try again," she said. Rowan looked at the bread. It had four flat sides. The cheese was round like a ball. Round things roll. That was why it slid off. So Rowan turned the round cheese into a square. He cut it with a safe knife. Now the cheese had four sides too.

The square cheese sat on the square bread. It did not roll. It did not slide. Rowan cut the sandwich into two triangles. A triangle has three sides. He counted them. "One, two, three!" He ate his sandwich and sang a happy song. Then he found a triangle cookie in his lunch box. "A surprise triangle!" said Rowan.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Cooper wanted his red ball to roll all the way to the toy house. He pushed it slow. The ball stopped. "Hmm," said Cooper. "Why did it stop?"

He tried again. He pushed the ball fast. The ball rolled and rolled. It went all the way to the toy house. "Fast makes it go far!" said Cooper. He clapped his hands. Then he rolled a big ball and a small ball. The big ball was too big for the door. The small ball went right in. "Small fits," said Cooper.

He sat down to rest. His toes were warm in his socks. He touched the window. It felt cold like ice. He pulled his toe back. "Brrr," he said. Then he smelled cookies. A sharp, sweet smell came from the kitchen. Cooper ran to find them. "Fast feet!" he said.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Isla wanted to find her soap. It was a new soap. Mama went to buy it today. Isla could not see it on the shelf.

"Use your nose," said Mama. "The soap smells like flowers." Isla sniffed with her nose. She smelled something sweet. She followed the smell. There it was, under the towel.

Isla touched the soap with her hands. It felt smooth. Mama turned on the water. Isla heard the splash with her ears. The soap popped in her mouth a tiny bit. "Yuck," said Isla. She made a face. "Soap is not for tasting," said Mama. Isla washed her hands and made them tidy. Then Mama kissed her soft cheek. Isla smiled. "My nose found the soap," she said.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Jasmine wanted to make a party for her teddy bear. She got out her paints. She had red, blue, and yellow paint.

She painted a red hat. She painted a blue hat. She painted a yellow hat. Then she wanted a green hat. But there was no green paint.

Jasmine looked and looked. "No green," she said. She made a dot of blue. She made a dot of yellow. The two dots touched. The paint turned green!

"Blue and yellow make green," said Jasmine. She dipped her brush again. More blue. More yellow. More green. She painted a big green hat, and it was her best one.

The paint had to dry. Jasmine waited. She waited slowly. She gave teddy a cracker because he looked hungry. She marched around the table one time. Then two times. She sat down and waited some more.

At last the hats were dry. Red, blue, yellow, and green. Jasmine put them on the table. She put the green one on teddy's head.

"Now we can have our party," she said.

activity: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
knowledge_domain: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
story:
Colton stood in the restaurant kitchen. The window was snowy and white. The cook gave him warm toast, soft butter, and a small pitcher of milk.

Colton spread the butter. The hard butter tore the toast. He looked at the warm toast. "Why does the butter tear it?" he asked. He held the toast near the stove. The toast got warmer. The butter went soft. Now it spread smooth like paint. "The warm toast makes soft butter," he said.

Next came the milk. Colton held the pitcher up high. The milk splashed out. It splashed like a turtle diving into a pond. He tried again. This time he kept the pitcher low, close to the cup. He poured slowly with two hands. Not one drop fell. He did it. "All the milk is in my cup," he said. He took a big drink.

activity: getting through an evening power cut at home
knowledge_domain: getting through an evening power cut at home
story:
The lights went out at the farmhouse. It was dark! Kai held Dad's hand. "Oh no!" said Kai.

Dad found a flashlight. Dad stepped across the kitchen floor. Click! The light came on. "A candle party!" said Dad. He lit one pretty candle. Mom put apples and crackers on a blanket. Kai laughed and clapped.

Kai wanted cold milk. He pulled the fridge door open. Dad ran over. "Shut it quick!" said Dad. "The cold will run out." Kai pushed the door shut. He waited. Then he opened it fast, grabbed the milk, and shut it again. "I did it!" said Kai. He drank his milk by the candle. Outside, the porch light popped back on. "The lights are home!" said Kai. Dad blew out the candle. "Goodnight, candle," said Kai.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Julia wants to play outside. She looks out the big window. The sun is not out today. Rain drops tap, tap, tap on the glass. Julia holds her yellow hat in her hands.

"Rainy day," says Julia. "I need my boots."

She counts what she needs. "One hat. Two boots. Three raincoat." The raincoat is red with white dots. It has a little triangle on the pocket. Julia puts it all on. It takes a long time. She pulls and wiggles each boot.

Mama opens the door. Puddles sit on the path like little ponds. Julia steps in one. Splash! Her socks stay dry inside the boots. "Dry feet," says Julia. She steps in another. Splash, splash!

Then the wind comes. It blows her yellow hat up, up, off her head. The hat lands in the bush. Julia waits. The wind slows down. She walks over slowly, slowly, and picks it up. She holds the hat on tight with both hands.

Julia looks up at the sky. Something soft and white falls on her nose. "Snowy!" says Julia. One snowflake, two snowflakes, three. Mama brings out warm mittens. Julia wears them and catches snow on her tongue. "Tasty," she says. "Cold and tasty." Then she waves at the snowy sky.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Felix found a book about crabs at daycare. Miss Ana said the book came from the library. Felix held it tight. He wanted to keep it forever.

Felix opened the book. He saw little black marks under the pictures. "What are those?" he asked. Miss Ana said, "Those are words. They tell the story." Felix turned the page. The crab was there. He turned more pages, one by one, all the way to the back. Then the story was done.

At snack time, Felix ate a salty cracker. He put the book next to his cubby. "This book is mine now," he said. Miss Ana shook her head. "The book needs to go back," she said. "It goes back on Friday. Then other kids can read it too."

Felix felt a surprise in his tummy. He did not want to give it up. He looked at the crab book. He looked at his friend Sam. Sam was looking at it too.

"Sam can look at it first," said Felix. He held the book open. "We start at the front," he said. Sam nodded. They turned the pages together, slow and slow, until the very end.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Connor sat down for dinner. He put his toy monkey on the chair too. "Monkey is hungry," said Connor. Dad gave Connor a bowl of peas. Connor held a pea up to the monkey's mouth. The pea rolled down and fell on the floor. Pip! Connor tried again. The pea fell again. Monkey did not chew. Monkey did not swallow.

Then Connor put the pea in his own mouth. Munch, munch, gone! Dad laughed. "Monkey is a toy," said Dad. "Toys do not eat. Foods are for eating." Connor looked at his plate. Peas were food. Banana slices were food. Monkey was not food. So Connor ate the banana all by himself.

"You wear a bib, and monkey gets nothing," said Dad. Connor picked up his fork. "Careful, that end is sharp," said Dad. Connor smiled and fed himself one big pea. "Peas fall down because monkey has no mouth that works," he said. Dad clapped. "My big boy eats the food, and the monkey just watches."

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Henry ran to the park with his dad. Yesterday it had rained. Today the sun was warm. "Where are the puddles?" Henry asked. All the wet spots were gone. The rain came yesterday, not today. That was why the ground was dry.

Henry wanted to splash, but there was no water. He felt a little angry. His sweater was too warm now, so Dad put it in the bag. They went down the slide. They dug in the sand. "Later we will get ice cream," said Dad. Henry had to wait until later. Waiting was hard, but he kept playing.

A truck drove by with a big water tank. It sprinkled the flowers near the fence. Water made a little pool on the path! Henry stomped his boots. Splash, splash. "New water today!" he laughed. Dad took a photo. "Tomorrow we can look at the picture and remember," he said. Henry clapped his wet hands.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Zoey sat at the dinner table. Her macaroni was warm and bumpy in her spoon. She wanted to show her father her picture. But his face looked down, and his mouth was a flat line.

Zoey looked at the cat clock. She looked at her father again. His eyebrows hung low. She had seen that face before. Her brother made it when his ice cream fell. "You are sad," Zoey said. Her father nodded. "My cup broke today," he said.

Zoey slid her picture across the table. It had a big yellow sun. "The sun makes me happy," she said. Her father looked at it. Then the corners of his mouth went up. Up, up, up, like a slide at the park. "Now you are happy!" said Zoey. She felt so excited she jumped in her seat. The dog came to chase the macaroni that fell. Everyone laughed, even Zoey's father, with his big smile.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Evelyn sat at the little table. She had paper and glue. She wanted to make a lion. She glued on a round yellow head. She glued on a tail.

Now the lion needed a mane. Evelyn picked up a red crayon. She pressed hard on the paper. Nothing showed. She pressed again. Still nothing. Her paper stayed white.

Evelyn tried the glue on the crayon. That did not work either. Then she saw the paint pots. She dipped a brush in orange paint. She touched the paper. Orange lines showed up! Wet paint sticks to paper, she thought. The crayon was dry, so it made no lines.

She painted a big orange mane. Round and round her brush went. The mane got bigger and bigger. "Look at my lion!" she said. Her teacher smiled. "What a big orange mane," she said. Evelyn held up her lion so everyone could see it.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Stella loves book day at daycare. The noisy bus takes them to the library. Stella finds a book about a red fox. She points at the marks under the fox. "What are those?" she asks. The marks are words, and the words tell the story. Stella turns the pages. She starts at the front. The fox is small at first. At the back, the fox is big. "The book goes front to back," she says.

Stella wants to keep the fox book forever. She hides it in her cubby. But Miss Kim looks for it. The book belongs to the library. You can borrow books and take them home. But you must bring them back by a certain day. Other people want to read them too.

Stella marches to the desk. She gives the book to the librarian. The librarian stamps a card with a big stamp. Stella borrows the book the right way. At home, she reads the fox story to her cat, front to back, with her pencil tucked behind her ear.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Layla sat on the rug. She wanted to build a tall tower. She put one block on another. "I have an idea," she said. "I will make it very tall!"

Then the big dog barked outside. Boom! The sound was loud. Layla felt scared. Her tummy felt tight. She dropped her blocks and ran to Mama.

Mama held her hand. They stood still. They waited. The dog went quiet. Layla's tummy felt different now. The scared feeling got small.

"Because the dog is quiet, I am not scared," said Layla.

She went back to the rug. She was excited to build again. She stacked the blocks slowly. One, two, three. The tower stood tall.

Layla smiled a big, happy smile. "Look, Mama! My tower!"

But then her little brother crawled over. He pushed the tower. Crash! The blocks fell down. Layla felt angry. Her face got hot.

She took a big breath. She waited. The angry feeling got small too.

Layla built the tower again. This time it was different. It was even taller.

activity: getting through an evening power cut at home
knowledge_domain: getting through an evening power cut at home
story:
The lights went out. The house went dark. Jules looked out the window. Snow was falling on the backyard. The snow looked white in the dark.

"Where is the light?" Jules asked. Dad said, "We need the flashlight." They looked in the big drawer. The flashlight was there. Jules clicked it on. But it made only a tiny beam. "Why is it so small?" Jules asked. Dad said, "The batteries are old." They put in new batteries. Jules clicked again. Now the light was big and real. It shone all the way to the fence.

Jules counted with the light. "One stone. Two stones. Three stones." Then he saw the bird bath. The light stopped on the ice. "Fish live in water," said Jules. "Do fish live in ice?" Dad laughed. "No, little fish swim far, far away." Jules shone the light up at the falling snow. Each snowflake glowed. "One, two, three, too many!" he said.

Dad made sandwiches by flashlight. Jules ate his on a blanket. He clicked the flashlight on and off. On, off, on. "The lights will come back," said Dad. Then the kitchen light blinked. It came back on. Jules waved his flashlight at the bulb. "Hi, big light," he said. "You found your batteries too."

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Aubrey woke up early at Grandma's house. She reached for her bunny. Bunny was not there. "I lost bunny," she said.

Grandma gave Aubrey a cup of milk. "Think," said Grandma. "Where did you play last?" Aubrey sipped her milk. Then she remembered. She had played in the garden. She had played with the watering can.

Aubrey ran to the garden. She looked by the flowers. No bunny. She looked under the bench. No bunny. Then she saw the watering can. It was lying on its side. Aubrey looked inside. There was bunny, all wet! "The water went in," said Aubrey. "The can fell over. That made bunny wet."

Grandma hung bunny on the line in the sun. "The sun will dry him," she said. Aubrey waited and waited. At last bunny was warm and dry. Aubrey hugged him tight. "Bunny, you can share my cookie," she said. Grandma smiled and cut the cookie in two.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Victoria was at the beach with her dad. Behind the sand was the little local pool. Victoria wanted to swim in it. But she could not swim yet.

First she sat on the pool step. The water came up to her tummy. Her dad held her hands. "Kick your legs," he said. Victoria kicked and kicked. But she stayed in one place. She tried again. Kick, kick, kick. Still no moving.

Then her dad said, "Try big slow kicks, not fast little ones." Victoria made one big slow kick. Then another. Her body moved forward through the water. She was swimming a little bit! "My big kicks make me go," she said.

After that, they took a break. They sat on the sand. The wind blew on Victoria's wet arms. She found a slimy green bit of seaweed and dropped it fast. Then they went back to the pool. Kick, kick, kick. Big and slow. Victoria moved all the way to the wall.

"I did it, Dad!" she said. "The water went splash, splash, splash."

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Mohamed sat at the kitchen table. He had paper, glue, and seeds. He wanted to make a flower picture for his mom.

First he put glue on the paper. Then he set the seeds on top. But the seeds slid down the paper. One seed fell off the table. Mohamed picked it up and put it back. It slid again.

Mohamed looked at his hands. The glue was wet and sticky on his fingers. "Wet glue makes things slip," he said. He held each seed in place. He counted to ten, slow and quiet. Then he let go. The seed stayed.

He made petals with the seeds, one by one. He made a stem with a green string. Mom came in with a clean cloth. She wiped his sticky hands. "A flower for me?" she asked. Mohamed nodded. He picked up the picture to show her. But the picture was heavy on one side. The seeds there were still wet. They slid to the corner of the page. Mohamed laughed. "Wet glue makes things slip," he said again. He laid the picture flat on the table. He put his hands on top, like a bird sitting on a nest. He counted to ten again.

The seeds stayed put. Mom hung the flower picture on the wall. "It can dry there," she said. Mohamed smiled and waved to his flower. "Stay there, little seeds," he said.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Ruby went to the garden center with Dad. She picked out little seeds. "Carrots," said Ruby. "And beans!" Dad got a big bag of soil. A noisy crow sat on the roof. "Caw, caw," it called.

At home, Ruby planted her seeds in two pots. She put one pot in the sun. She put the other pot in the sun too. Every day, Ruby watered one pot. "Grow, grow, little seeds," she said. The other pot got no water at all.

Soon a tiny green leaf came up. Then two leaves. Then three. Ruby clapped her hands. But the dry pot had nothing. Not one leaf. The soil was hard and cracked. Ruby touched it. "Oh," she said. "This pot is so dry." She thought and thought. "The dry pot has no water. That is why nothing grows." She gave it a big drink.

Day by day, Ruby watered both pots. "Grow, grow, little seeds," she said. The first new leaf peeked out at last. Ruby smiled and called to Dad, "Come see! Water helped it live!"

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Carter wanted his toy pig. It was on the big counter. The pot on the stove was making steam. "Is it hot up there?" he wondered.

Carter reached up with his hand. Grandma held his arm. "Stay close to me," she said. "The pot is hot. The pot can hurt you."

Carter touched the cold fridge instead. "Ooh, this one is cold," he said. "The pot is hot. The fridge is cold. They are different!" The steam moved up, up, up. Carter watched it go.

Then Grandma got the pig down for him. She put it in the sink. The sink was warm and soapy. Carter washed his pig with bubbles. "Pig was dirty," he said. "Now pig is clean. The soap made him clean!"

Grandma smiled. "Yes it did," she said. "Now let's dry him with the soft towel."

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Felix stood in the band room. He held a small trumpet. He wanted to make a big sound. He blew air into it. Nothing came out but air.

The teacher sat next to him. "Try again," she said. "Take your time."

Felix blew again. Still no sound. He felt upset. A bird sat on the window and looked in.

The teacher smiled. "Watch me," she said. She made her lips buzz like a bee. Then the trumpet sang out loud.

Felix buzzed his lips. He put them on the trumpet. He blew. The trumpet sang!

"It buzzed because my lips buzzed!" said Felix. He did it again. And again. He did not stop.

The bird on the window flew up. It climb higher and higher. Then it sang too.

Felix played one more song, nice and slow.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Milo went to the library with his mom. The library was busy. Lots of kids were reading. Milo found a book about a dog. The dog chased a ball up to a tree. The dog chased a cat, too. Milo loved this book.

He sat down on a small red chair. He opened the book. The words were on every page. "Dog," Milo read. He knew that word. The words told about the dog. He turned page one, then page two. He read all the way to the end. The front came first, and the back came last.

"I want to keep this book," Milo said. "Forever and ever."

Mom shook her head. "We can take it home," she said. "Then we bring it back."

Milo held the book tight. He did not want to let go.

The next week, Milo came back to the library. A girl sat in the red chair. She had his dog book. She turned the pages, one by one.

"That is my book," Milo said.

"It was yours," said the girl. "Now it is mine."

Mom smiled. "And after her, it can be yours again."

Milo watched the girl read. He waited. She read slow. She read to the very last page. Then she closed the book and gave it back.

Milo took it. He opened the front page. "Dog," he read again. He was happy to start at the beginning. "My turn," he said.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Logan stood at the hotel pool. He held Dad's hand tight. "The water is big," Logan said. "I will hold you," said Dad. Logan stepped down the steps. The water was warm on his toes.

Logan saw a girl floating on her back. Her arms were out wide. Her tummy was up like a boat. She looked so calm. Logan wanted to try. Dad held his back in the water. "Take a big breath," said Dad. "Put your tummy up." Logan took a big breath. His tummy went up. His legs came up too. He was floating! "Air in my tummy makes me float!" Logan said. He saw the blue color of the sky above him.

Dad kept one hand under him, just in case. Logan splashed a little with his hands. The water made tickly sounds by his ears. A cute little duck toy floated past him. "Look, it floats too," said Logan. Dad laughed. "You and the duck," said Dad. Logan kicked his feet gently and stayed floating. Then Dad lifted him up for a warm towel hug.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Cooper went to the big game with Mom and Dad. The ice was white and shiny. A big robot mascot walked around and waved. Cooper wore his red shirt to match his team. His team was the red team, and red was his best color.

Cooper wanted to see the puck. But the seats were full of tall people. "I can't see!" he said. Then everyone cheered. The red team scored a goal! But Cooper missed it. Everyone had stood up. When people cheer, they stand up. That is why he could not see.

So Cooper got ready. He watched the red team skate fast. He heard the crowd begin to roar. Quick, quick, up he climbed onto Dad's shoulders! The red team scored again. This time Cooper saw the puck go in. He saw the robot do a happy dance. "We saw it!" Cooper shouted. "We saw it!" The smelly old skates in his bag did not matter now. He waved his red flag high, high, high.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Grayson went to the playground with Mom. He wanted to go on the big slide. Mom said, "Keep close to me." Grayson held her hand. The sun was warm on his face.

Near the slide there was a metal bench. Grayson put his hand on it. He pulled his hand back fast. The bench was hot! The sun made it hot. "The sun made it hot," Grayson said. Mom touched it too. "Yes, the sun is real and strong today," she said. "Hot things can hurt. Let's find the shady slide."

They found the little slide under a tree. It felt cool and smooth. Grayson slid down, one, two, three times. He laughed and laughed.

Then Grayson saw something shiny in the grass. It was a broken bottle. "Don't touch," said Mom softly. "Sharp glass can hurt." Grayson kept his hands behind his back. Mom picked it up with a bag. Then it was time for pizza under the shady tree. Grayson ate a real big slice. "Hot bench, cool slide, safe hands," he said. Mom smiled and kissed his head.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
story:
Jaxon ran to the gate. Grandpa was here! Grandpa had a big bag. "I will stay for a week," said Grandpa. Jaxon did not know how long a week was. Was it as long as a nap? "Grandpa, what is a week?" he asked. "It is seven days," said Grandpa. "Seven!" said Jaxon.

Grandpa gave Jaxon a rubber snake. It was long and green. "Are you afraid of it?" asked Grandpa. "No!" said Jaxon. "It is a toy." Jaxon made the snake hop in the grass. Grandpa laughed and they went out to play.

Each morning Jaxon put one stone in a jar. One stone. Two stones. Three. The jar got more full each day. On the seventh morning, the jar was full. "The jar is full," said Jaxon. "Seven days went by!" Grandpa picked up his big bag. "I will come back soon," he said. Jaxon waved and waved until the car went down the road.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story: Sienna sat in a big chair at Grandma's house. Grandma had a little salon in the back room. It had a mirror and a sink. Today Sienna would get her very first haircut. "Do not cut it all off!" said Sienna. Grandma laughed. "I only take little bits. Snip, snip, little snip." First Grandma sprayed water on Sienna's head. "Why is my hair wet?" asked Sienna. "Wet hair lies down flat," said Grandma. "Flat hair is easy to cut." Sienna touched her wet hair. It was not puffy anymore. It lay down like a sleepy cat. "My hair went flat because of the water," said Sienna. "That is right, smart girl," said Grandma. Then came the scissors. Snip, snip, little snip. Sienna watched the mirror. A tiny piece of hair fell down. It landed on her bib like a small brown mountain. "Look, Grandma! A hair mountain!" said Sienna. Grandma kept cutting. Snip, snip, little snip. Then Grandma held up the mirror so Sienna could see the back. Sienna held her teddy bear tight and looked. Her hair was short and neat and still there. "You did not cut it all off," said Sienna. "I told you," said Grandma. "Only little bits." Sienna patted her head. "Hair mountain, flat hair, little bits," she said. "Now we look pretty together," said Grandma, spinning the chair round and round. "Again!" said Sienna. "Spin me again!"

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
story:
Jacob ran into the kitchen. "Pasta!" he yelled. "Pasta, pasta, pasta!"

He grabbed his fork. He was ready to eat. But Mama put her hand on the bowl. "Wait," she said. "We say the blessing first."

Jacob looked out the window. White snow was falling on the trees. He looked at his plate. "But I want pasta now," he said.

"Watch me," said Mama. She folded her arms. Grandma folded her arms. Big sister Lily folded her arms. Jacob folded his arms too. They went like this: one arm, then the other arm.

"Dear God," said Mama. "Thank you for our food. Thank you for snow to play in. Amen."

"Amen!" said Jacob. It was a big word. He said it loud.

Then Mama picked up the bowl. Steam went up, up, up. It smelled warm and cheesy. Jacob skipped to his chair, one, two, three skips.

There was broccoli on his plate too. "That is ugly broccoli," said Jacob.

"Eat one tree," said Grandma. "Just one."

Jacob ate it. Then he ate all his pasta. "We bless first," he said. "Then we eat!"

Grandma smiled. "That's right, big boy."

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Lillian lost her bunny. Bunny was soft and gray. Lillian wanted to find him.

"Where are you, Bunny?" she said. First she looked under the bed. No bunny there. One. Then she looked in the toy box. No bunny there. Two. Then she looked by the big chair. No bunny there. Three.

Lillian sat down on the rug. She thought hard. "Where did I play with Bunny last?" she said. "I played with Bunny in my bed. Then I got up to get my shirt."

Lillian went back to her bed. She pulled the blanket back. Bunny was hiding under the pillow! He had been there the whole time. "The blanket was on top of you," Lillian said. "That is why I could not see you."

Lillian hugged Bunny close. "Now you can sleep with me," she said. She tucked Bunny under her warm blanket. His little ears felt cold, so she covered them too.

"Good night, Bunny," Lillian said. "One hug, and one more."

"Sleep tight, little bunny."

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Penelope went out to the backyard. She wanted to paint a picture of her red apple. She put the apple on the grass. She got her paints and a clean brush.

She looked for red paint. The red pot was empty. "Oh no," she said. She found blue paint and yellow paint. She put some blue on her brush. She painted the apple. It looked all blue. That was not right.

She dipped her brush in the yellow pot too. She painted on top of the blue. The apple turned green! Penelope blinked. She touched the green paint with her finger. "Blue and yellow make green," she said. "The blue did it. Then the yellow did it too."

She painted big green leaves all around her apple. Then she painted the sky blue above it. A soft wind moved the paper. Penelope picked up her broom. She gave the patio a little sweep to clean the paint drips. Then she held up her picture to the sun. "Look, apple," she said. "Now you have green leaves."

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
story:
Livia ran to the door. "Is it shot day?" she asked. Mom said yes. Livia loved the doctor's sticker prize at the end. But she did not love the shot.

At the office, the nurse typed on her computer. "You are next," she said. Livia held her teddy tight. She squeezed her arm into a hard ball. "Ow!" The nurse said, "Try a soft arm. A tight arm makes it hurt more." Livia let her arm go soft like a noodle. Quick quick, the shot was done! "It was small," said Livia. "My arm was soft, so it was small."

Mom clapped. The nurse gave her a bandage and a shiny star sticker. Livia held it up high. "Next time I will make my arm soft too!" she said. Then she ran to the toy corner, fast as a rabbit.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Cooper ran onto the soccer field. The grass was still wet. His team had red shirts. Cooper liked his red shirt a lot.

"Time to play," said Coach May. She looked at Cooper's legs. "Where are your shin guards?" Cooper looked down. He had socks, but no guards under them. "No guards, no playing," said Coach May. "A kick can hurt your legs."

Cooper sat on the bench. He watched his friend Sam kick the ball. Sam ran fast. Sam drank water at the break. Cooper wanted to run too.

Then Mom came running. She had Cooper's shin guards in her bag. "You left them in the car," she said. Cooper slid them on under his socks. "Guards on, playing on," he said. Coach May smiled.

Cober ran onto the field. He kicked the ball. It went into the net! "I can play because my guards are on," Cooper said. He kicked the ball again, pretty and far, all the way to Sam.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
Today Hudson turned three. His family had a party at the bowling alley. Grandma held his hand. Hudson wore red bowling shoes. On his score card, he draws a big round ball with his crayon. It was his turn. He wanted to knock down all the pins.

Hudson rolled his ball, but it rolled very slowly. It stopped in the middle of the lane. Not one pin fell down. "Problem," said Hudson. He looked at his ball. It stopped because it was too slow. Daddy said, "Want to try again?" Hudson picked up a new ball. This time he pushed it hard with both hands.

The ball rolled fast, fast, fast. Crash! Six pins fell down. Everyone clapped. "It went fast because I pushed hard," said Hudson. Grandma gave him a hug. Then the cake came, with three candles. Hudson blew them all out. "Happy birthday to you," everyone sang. Hudson sat close to Grandma. He felt safe and happy. He ate his cake and smiled.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Jaxon sat in the family car. "We are going to the salon," said Mom. "You will get your first haircut."

At the salon, a lady named Bea put a cape on Jaxon. The cape was like a big bib. Bea picked up her scissors. Snip, snip. One snip, two snips.

Little bits of hair fell down. They landed on the cape. They did not stick to Jaxon. The cape caught them, like it catches everything.

Jaxon watched in the mirror. A light made his hair shine. He saw a bit of hair fall. He touched his head. It did not hurt at all. "The hair is not on me anymore," he said. "The cape caught it because it is wide." Bea smiled. "That is right. The cape keeps you clean."

Mom had an egg sandwich in her bag for later. Jaxon got to share it after the haircut. He took a bite and smiled. "I like my haircut," said Jaxon. "Snip, snip," said Bea. "One happy boy, all done."

Jaxon looked in the mirror one more time. "Nice hair," he said.
